DESCRIPTION: LED-136 (2026-09-26) added a live exchange-rate feed and converted the Budgets spend into the default currency. Income, expense and category totals elsewhere are still mixed-currency sums, so with a foreign account two screens can disagree by a factor of 60 (Budgets 89.44 against a pie that says 5,600). This epic converts the remaining totals, closes the smaller gaps the LED-136 retro listed, and runs the live checks it could not. Source: knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-136-exchange-rate-feed.md. Phases and the decision register are in epics-15-19-build-order.md.

SUMMARY: Income and expense totals are converted into the default currency
USER_STORY: As a user with a foreign-currency account, I want income and expense totals in one currency, so the numbers on Home and Reports can be compared with Budgets.
DESCRIPTION: `sumTransactionsByType` (src/hooks/useDashboardData.ts:190) adds native amounts. `amountInCurrency` (src/lib/exchangeRates.ts:122) already returns the converted amount or `null` when there is no rate. Found by LED-136 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-136-exchange-rate-feed.md). Observed: With a foreign account, Budgets shows the converted spend and the Home pie beside it does not (live: 89.44 against 5,600). Suggested fix: One pure helper in `src/lib` that converts income and expense rows into the default currency once and returns the total plus the rows it had to leave out (no rate), so every caller says what is missing instead of guessing (`rules/foreign-currency-rate-of-one-is-not-a-rate.md`). Do not import the `@/` alias or a hook, so `node --test` can load it.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) One helper, in `src/lib`, with unit tests for: same currency, converted, an override rate, and a row with no rate (left out and counted); (b) Home income, expense and net for a foreign account equal the converted sum; (c) a row with no rate is named, never counted at 1; (d) totals for a single-currency user do not change; (e) lint, build and tests pass.

SUMMARY: Category breakdown, Reports flows and Top categories use the converted totals
USER_STORY: As a user, I want the category pie, the Reports flows and Top categories to agree with each other and with Budgets, so one number means one thing.
DESCRIPTION: src/lib/categoryBreakdown.ts (`buildCategoryBreakdown`), `summarizeRange` used by src/pages/ReportsPage.tsx, the Home expense pie and cash flow in src/hooks/useDashboardData.ts, and src/components/transactions/FilterTopCategories.tsx. Found by LED-136 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-136-exchange-rate-feed.md) and LED-149 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-149-density-leftovers.md). Observed: Reports and the pie still add native amounts. Top categories counts one currency (the one with the most expenses) and says so, because a multi-currency filter had no combined view. Suggested fix: Move every caller onto the LED-182 helper and drop the one-currency workaround in Top categories once a combined view exists; keep the note only for rows left out.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Home pie, cash flow, Reports summary, category breakdown and Top categories all read the LED-182 helper; (b) with a foreign account the pie total equals the Budgets spend to the cent; (c) Top categories with two expense currencies shows one combined list and names any row left out; (d) tests for the breakdown with a converted row and a missing-rate row; (e) totals for a single-currency user do not change.

SUMMARY: Net worth over time walks back in the default currency
USER_STORY: As a user with a foreign account, I want the net worth chart to use one currency, so the history matches the number at its right edge.
DESCRIPTION: `netWorthData` in src/pages/ReportsPage.tsx. Found by LED-136 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-136-exchange-rate-feed.md). Observed: It walks back from today's converted net worth using native transaction amounts, so a foreign account mixes currencies (it did before too, in the other direction). LED-143 left this unwinding alone (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-143-deletion-export.md). Suggested fix: Convert each transaction with `amountInCurrency` before subtracting it, and leave out and name rows with no rate.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) The first point of the chart equals today's net worth and each earlier point differs by the converted amount; (b) a row with no rate is named; (c) a unit test for the walk-back with a foreign account; (d) a single-currency user sees the same chart as before.

SUMMARY: Cross-currency transfers get a second rate, and Overspending totals stop adding currencies
USER_STORY: As a user who moves money between currencies, I want the two sides of a transfer to be valued, so balances and Overspending are right.
DESCRIPTION: Item (f) and item (e) of the LED-136 ticket, neither in the approved plan (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-136-exchange-rate-feed.md). Observed: A transfer between two currencies carries one amount; the receiving side has no rate of its own. The Overspending card can print a mixed-currency "A + B" total. Suggested fix: Store the destination amount or rate on the transfer, and print Overspending in the default currency with the LED-182 helper. This needs a data-model choice, so it is decision OD-10. Fallback: transfers keep one amount and Overspending shows one line per currency, labelled. Decision (2026-10-03, OD-10): (a), store the destination amount on the transfer (migration).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) OD-10 answered in the decision register; (b) a cross-currency transfer changes both balances by the amounts the user sees; (c) a migration (if any) applies to an empty database and passes the CI `db` job; (d) Overspending shows no "A + B" total; (e) tests.

SUMMARY: Deletion export gives budgets their converted spend
USER_STORY: As a user exporting my data, I want the budgets file to show foreign-currency spend, so "Spent" matches the app.
DESCRIPTION: The Data deletion page export of budgets (src/lib, see LED-143). Found by LED-136 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-136-exchange-rate-feed.md) and LED-143 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-143-deletion-export.md). Observed: The export has no rates, so foreign-currency spend is left out of its "Spent" column. `useBudgets` returns active budgets only and does a 13-month spend read the export does not need, so inactive budgets are not exported. Suggested fix: Pass the converter to the builder; read inactive budgets for the export only. Wording and scope of the export are LED-180 and are not decided here.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) "Spent" in the budgets CSV equals the Budgets page for a foreign account; (b) inactive budgets are included, marked as inactive; (c) a unit test for the builder with a converted and a no-rate row; (d) the file still names itself with the local date.

SUMMARY: Settings rate status says "fetched" when nothing was requested
USER_STORY: As a user, I want the rates status to say what happened, so I can tell a fetch from a skip.
DESCRIPTION: src/components/settings/ExchangeRatesCard.tsx (`fetchedLabel`). Found by LED-136 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-136-exchange-rate-feed.md). Observed: The status reads "Rates · fetched …" when no currency needed a fetch and nothing was requested. Suggested fix: Say "Rates · nothing to fetch" (or hide the time) when no rate was requested; keep the time when one was.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) With only the base currency in use the status does not claim a fetch; (b) with a foreign account the fetched time still shows; (c) a test on the label function.

SUMMARY: Live checks the exchange-rate ticket could not run
USER_STORY: As a maintainer, I want the untested refresh paths run against a real database, so the feed is known to work in each mode.
DESCRIPTION: LED-136 listed what only unit tests covered (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-136-exchange-rate-feed.md). Method: `knowledge/patterns/browser-check-with-local-user.md` and `live-sweep-method.md`. Items: (1) `every time I open` and `weekly` refresh live; (2) the offline queue with `original_amount` (queue a foreign expense offline, reconnect, compare the stored amounts); (3) an import of transfers between currencies; (4) `every time I open` with the feed blocked (the app falls back to "no rate: left out of totals"). Record each as PASS, FAIL or not checkable in a retro; a FAIL becomes a new ticket.
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) Each item has a result in knowledge/retros/2026-MM-DD-live-sweep-currency.md; (b) each FAIL has a ticket id; (c) measured values for (2); (d) no live account touched.

SUMMARY: Legal pages: Privacy Policy, Terms, data deletion, cookies and storage, and other legal notices
USER_STORY: As a visitor, I want the policy to say which third parties the app contacts, so I can decide with the facts.
DESCRIPTION: src/pages (Privacy Policy) and the LED-88 legal copy. Found by LED-136 (knowledge/retros/2026-09-26-led-136-exchange-rate-feed.md). Observed: The policy lists Google and Supabase as third parties. Since LED-136 the browser also contacts `api.frankfurter.dev`, which receives currency codes and the visitor's IP. This is legal text: the product owner approves the wording before it is committed (OD-9; same rule as OD-5). Fallback: the policy is unchanged and the gap is recorded here. Decision (2026-10-03, OD-9): widened by the owner. Write up the Privacy Policy (naming every third party the browser contacts: Supabase, Google sign-in, api.frankfurter.dev, Google Fonts), the Terms and Conditions, the data deletion instructions, a cookie and browser-storage notice (what Ledger keeps in localStorage and why; no tracking or advertising cookies), and the other notices a self-hosted finance app needs (not financial advice, self-hosting operator responsibilities, open-source licence, contact). The cookie and storage settings screen is LED-245. Legal text: the owner approves every page's wording before it is committed (OD-5).
ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA: (a) The owner approves the wording of each page before it is committed (OD-9, OD-5); (b) the Privacy Policy names every host the browser contacts and what each receives; (c) Terms, data deletion instructions and the cookie and storage notice are written and linked from the legal pages and the login footer; (d) every changed page shows a new "last updated" date; (e) statements match the code (the stored keys, the hosts in the CSP, the deletion flow), checked against the source.
